storm.summary_layperson: No storm risk tonight — radar is clear, there's essentially no fuel for thunderstorms to form, and any isolated showers well to the west over New York should stay clear of the cove.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer in play — Sound water (75.9°F) and air (75.2°F) are within a degree of each other, so there's no stabilizing gap, though there's also nothing approaching that would need one.
storm.detail_html:
Nothing is on KOKX radar approaching the cove this evening — no storm cells tracked, no active NWS alerts. CAPE (a measure of atmospheric fuel for thunderstorms) is essentially negligible at 70 J/kg now and the HRRR model forecasts it dropping to 0 J/kg by mid-evening. Bulk shear is a healthy 32 kt out of the west, but shear only organizes storms when there's instability to work with, and there isn't.

NWS's afternoon discussion (OKX, issued 2:32 PM) notes some lingering moisture and instability (500–1500 J/kg SBCAPE) well to the west over the Lower Hudson Valley, NE NJ, and NYC that could support isolated-to-scattered showers and storms there, but explicitly calls the shear weak enough that no severe impacts are expected — and that activity is not tracking toward western LIS.

The Sound's marine layer (the stable air pocket that normally chokes storms crossing the water) isn't a factor either way tonight: water (75.9°F) and air (75.2°F, cooling toward the upper 60s by early morning) are within about a degree of each other, so there's no meaningful gap to stabilize the air. It's a moot point this evening since nothing is inbound to need it.

Most likely outcome for the 5–10 PM window: dry, partly sunny skies, light NE gradient wind, no thunderstorm risk. What would change the call: a new cell developing over the Hudson Valley/NYC corridor and tracking east-northeast toward western LIS, or radar returns appearing within 50 mi of the cove.

wind.regime_label: Light gradient wind — no sea breeze, direction may wander

hourly.shift_note: veering back to ENE, going lighter
light and wandering, may go variable

wind.tactics_blurb: Light NE gradient flow all evening, generally uniform across the cove — no sea breeze building tonight since inland air is barely different from the Sound's water temperature. Expect drifter conditions (4–7 kt) with a direction that may wander; RYC is currently reading a light SE eddy that should resolve back toward the broader NE flow.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
This is a gradient-only evening, not a sea-breeze day: the air–water temperature difference (deltaT) is –0.7°F — inland air is actually a hair cooler than the Sound — far short of the 5°F gap a thermal sea breeze needs to build. The regional gradient wind itself is light, averaging 6.5 kt across well-sited stations, which puts tonight in the light-gradient bucket: no sea breeze in play, and direction can wander rather than settle into a clean sea-breeze axis.

HRRR has the wind coming from ENE to NE (35–66°) through the window, which per the cove's geography is close to the cleanest offshore-style flow — laminar and relatively uniform across the course, so there isn't a strong case for favoring one shore over the other tonight; call it a wash slightly favoring mid-cove.

Station agreement is soft (direction_agreement 0.70 overall, just 0.56 across the western-LIS cluster), and RYC itself is currently reading SE at 142°/5.1 kt — about 100° off the broader NE ensemble median. That's a big enough gap to flag as a local eddy or terrain-driven shelter at the cove mouth rather than a real signal of a different regional wind; expect it to resolve back toward the NE gradient rather than persist.

What this feels like on the water: 4–7 kt with gusts to 6–10 kt is drifter territory — fine for light-air specialists, marginal for anything that needs pressure to plane. If it settles into the lighter end of the range after 8 PM, RC may be watching for a postponement threshold rather than running a full series.
